P002-D001.title: Diabetes check and risk factors
P002-D001.text:
Patient Gerald Wimmer, born 23.05.1970, male. Routine check.
Diagnoses: type 2 diabetes (since 2016, last HbA1c 7.8%), arterial hypertension (since 2018).
Medication: metformin 1000 mg 1-0-1, ramipril 5 mg 1-0-0.
Smoker: about 20 cigarettes/day since age 18 (about 36 pack-years).
BP 148/92, pulse 78/min. Weight 94 kg, height 178 cm, BMI 29.7.
Lipids (07/2019): total cholesterol 5.8 mmol/l, LDL 3.7 mmol/l, HDL 0.9 mmol/l, TG 2.4 mmol/l – dyslipidaemia!
HbA1c 8.1% – not at target.
ECG: sinus rhythm, signs of LVH, no ischaemia pattern.
Recommendation: continue metformin, dose adjustment discussed. Continue ramipril. Statin therapy strongly recommended – patient declines "for now", wants to try diet. Smoking cessation recommended.
Family history: father died of a heart attack at 61.
No known allergies.

P002-D002.title: Exercise ECG for suspected coronary artery disease
P002-D002.text:
Referred by Dr Holzmann for suspected coronary artery disease (exertional pain in the right shoulder).
Patient Wimmer Gerald, born 23.05.1970.

Previous illnesses: type 2 diabetes, arterial hypertension, dyslipidaemia (no statin so far), smoker.
Family history: father with myocardial infarction at 61.

Exercise ECG (bicycle):
Maximum load: 125 W (stopped because of exhaustion).
Max HR: 151/min. Max BP: 182/100.
ECG under load: ST depression 1.2 mm in V4–V6 at 100 W → suspected exercise-induced ischaemia.
No angina during the test.

Assessment: positive exercise test. Cardiology check and possibly coronary angiography recommended.
Stopping smoking strongly recommended.
Recommendation: start aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0 (GP), refer to cardiology.

P002-D003.title: Emergency referral for chest pain
P002-D003.text:
Emergency referral!
Patient: Wimmer Gerald, born 23.05.1970
Referral diagnosis: suspected acute coronary syndrome / STEMI

History: severe pressing chest pain for about 3 h, radiating to the left arm, sweating, nausea. Onset about 04:30.
Previous illnesses: type 2 diabetes, arterial hypertension, dyslipidaemia, suspected coronary artery disease (positive exercise ECG 03/2022, no coronary angiography done).
Medication: metformin 1000 mg 1-0-1, ramipril 5 mg 1-0-0, aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0.
Smoker (20 cigarettes/day).
Allergies: none known.

ECG in the practice: ST elevation in II, III, aVF – suspected inferior wall STEMI! Please admit immediately.
Aspirin 500 mg already given.
Dr Petra Holzmann

P002-D004.title: Admission report, chest pain unit
P002-D004.text:
Admission: 14.10.2024, 08:20, chest pain unit
Patient: Wimmer Gerald, born 23.05.1970, male

Referral diagnosis: suspected inferior wall STEMI.

History:
Pressing chest pain since about 04:30, radiating to the left arm, sweating, nausea. Pain at admission NRS 5/10 (somewhat better after aspirin 500 mg in the practice).

Previous illnesses:
- Type 2 diabetes (since 2016)
- Arterial hypertension
- Dyslipidaemia
- Positive exercise ECG 03/2022, no invasive tests done
- Smoking (20 cigarettes/day, about 36 pack-years)
No known allergies. No known previous surgery.

Physical examination:
General condition: moderate, in pain, sweating. Weight 96 kg, height 178 cm.
Heart: sounds regular, no murmurs. Pulse 92/min.
Lungs: vesicular both sides, no crackles.
Abdomen: soft, normal.
Limbs: no oedema.
BP 156/94 mmHg.

ECG at admission (08:22):
ST elevation II, III, aVF max 1.8 mm, reciprocal ST depression in I, aVL → inferior wall STEMI?
V4–V6: no significant ST elevation.

Note: ECG will be reviewed again by the senior doctor.

Diagnosis (provisional): suspected ACS, differential: inferior wall STEMI vs NSTEMI.

Plan:
- Troponin, CK, CK-MB, blood count, coagulation, basic chemistry stat
- Continuous monitoring
- Heparin 5,000 IU IV bolus
- Nitroglycerin sublingual for pain
- Senior doctor review immediately
- Prepare cardiac catheter lab

P002-D005.title: Emergency laboratory for ACS
P002-D005.text:
Patient: Wimmer Gerald, born 23.05.1970, male
Order number: LM-2024-10-14-0031
Sample taken: 14.10.2024, 08:30 (STAT)

Troponin T hs: 1,840 ng/l [ref: <14] ↑↑↑ → significantly raised
CK: 680 U/l [ref: <190] ↑↑
CK-MB: 62 U/l [ref: <25] ↑↑
LDH: 312 U/l [ref: <248] ↑

Blood count:
  Hb: 14.2 g/dl [ref: 13.5–17.5]
  Leucocytes: 11.8 G/l [ref: 4.0–10.0] ↑ (stress reaction)
  Platelets: 188 G/l [ref: 150–400]

Coagulation:
  INR: 1.04, aPTT: 28 s

Clinical chemistry:
  Na: 140 mmol/l, K: 4.0 mmol/l
  Creatinine: 1.08 mg/dl [ref: 0.7–1.2]
  eGFR: 74 ml/min/1.73m²
  Glucose: 9.8 mmol/l [ref: 3.9–6.1] ↑ (diabetes, stress)
  HbA1c: 8.6% ↑ [ref: <5.7%]
  Total cholesterol: 6.1 mmol/l, LDL: 4.0 mmol/l ↑

Comment: troponin rise consistent with myocardial damage. STAT result.

P002-D006.title: Senior doctor ECG review – reclassified as NSTEMI
P002-D006.text:
14.10.2024, 09:15, Senior Dr Bernhard Reithofer, cardiology

ECG review:
The admission ECG was interpreted by the GP as suspected STEMI; senior doctor review now:
ST elevation in II, III, aVF <2 mm, not a complete STEMI picture. Rather ST changes from inferior wall ischaemia without full STEMI criteria.
Troponin T hs: 1,840 ng/l – significantly raised → ACS confirmed.
Reclassification: NSTEMI (inferior wall ischaemia).

Plan: urgent coronary angiography within 24 h. Cardiac catheter lab booked for 14:00 today.
Simvastatin 40 mg 0-0-1 started (statin loading before the procedure).
Continue heparin (infusion, aPTT-guided).
Metformin PAUSED from now (contrast medium planned, kidney protection).
Nicotine patch 14 mg offered – patient agrees.

P002-D007.title: Nursing report, day of admission
P002-D007.text:
14.10.2024, 11:00, registered nurse Werner Stein

Mr Wimmer, chest pain unit bed 2. Monitoring running. Pain better, NRS 2/10.
In the nursing talk the patient reports that years ago he received iodinated contrast medium and became "all red in the face and short of breath". It went away by itself. This was passed on to the ward doctor.
Smoking: smoker, patch applied.
Glucose monitoring: 11.2 mmol/l. Insulin correction according to protocol.
BP 148/88, pulse 88/min. SpO2 98%.
Patient cooperative, understands the situation. Anxious about the upcoming cardiac catheter procedure.
Nil by mouth from 12:00 as ordered.

P002-D008.title: Preparation for coronary angiography – contrast allergy check
P002-D008.text:
14.10.2024, 13:30, Dr Sandra Krenn

Nursing report of a previous contrast reaction: the patient reports flushing and shortness of breath after iodinated contrast (date unknown). Resolved spontaneously. No anaphylaxis treatment needed at the time.
Discussed with radiology and anaesthesia:
→ Suspected mild contrast intolerance (pseudo-allergic reaction, grade I–II Ring/Messmer)
→ Premedication before contrast: prednisolone 50 mg orally now and 6 h before the procedure, clemastine 2 mg IV 30 min before
→ Use iso-osmolar contrast (iodixanol)
→ Emergency readiness in the catheter lab

First dose of simvastatin 40 mg given at noon.
Heparin infusion running, aPTT 64 s (target 60–80 s) → dose OK.

P002-D009.title: Coronary angiography + PCI (LAD stent)
P002-D009.text:
Cardiac catheter report
Date: 14.10.2024, 14:30–15:45
Operator: Senior Dr Klaus Brandner, interventional cardiologist
Assistant: Dr Sandra Krenn

Indication: NSTEMI, urgent coronary angiography.
Access: right radial artery, 6F.
Contrast: iodixanol (iso-osmolar), premedication given. Contrast tolerance: no reaction.

Coronary angiography findings:
- Left coronary artery: LAD: severe proximal stenosis (about 85%), TIMI 1 flow. LCX: minor wall irregularities, nothing significant.
- RCA: moderate stenosis (about 50%) in the middle segment, no intervention needed.

Decision: intervention on the LAD.

PCI:
Pre-dilatation with a 2.5 mm balloon. Drug-eluting stent (DES) in the proximal LAD: Orsiro Mission 3.0 × 18 mm (Biotronik, sirolimus-coated). Post-dilatation with a 3.5 mm balloon. Result: TIMI 3 flow, no residual stenosis. No dissection.

Complications: none.
Blood loss: minimal.
After the procedure:
- P2Y12 loading: ticagrelor 180 mg loading dose immediately after the procedure (class I, ESC ACS guideline).
- Stop heparin infusion this evening.

Diagnosis:
1. NSTEMI with LAD stenosis (I21.4)
2. Two-vessel coronary artery disease (LAD critical, RCA moderate)
3. Status after PCI with DES in the LAD, 14.10.2024

P002-D010.title: Progress note, day 1 after PCI
P002-D010.text:
15.10.2024, 07:30, Dr Krenn
Day 1 after PCI.

Patient awake, no symptoms. Pain 0/10. No chest pain.
Puncture site right wrist: dressing dry, no haematoma.
Pulse 72/min regular, BP 138/84, SpO2 99%.
ECG: sinus rhythm, ST normalised, small Q waves II/III/aVF → inferior infarction confirmed.

Simvastatin 40 mg started yesterday: after discussion with the senior doctor, switch to atorvastatin 80 mg 0-0-1 recommended (more effective in coronary disease after ACS, guideline-based). Simvastatin stopped.
Atorvastatin 80 mg 0-0-1 from today.

Dual antiplatelet therapy: continue aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0 and ticagrelor 90 mg 1-0-1.
Continue ramipril 5 mg.
Metformin: keep paused (contrast <48 h ago). Restart planned tomorrow if creatinine is stable.
Continue nicotine patch.

Plan:
- Echo today
- Lab tomorrow
- Smoking cessation advice
- Restart metformin tomorrow if creatinine OK

P002-D011.title: Echocardiography after NSTEMI
P002-D011.text:
Echocardiography report, 15.10.2024
Senior Dr Reithofer

Indication: NSTEMI after PCI – assessment of LV function.

Findings:
- LV: EF about 45% (mildly reduced). Regional wall motion abnormality: hypokinesia inferior and infero-posterior (matching inferior ischaemia).
- RV: normal.
- Valves: no significant pathology.
- No pericardial effusion.
- LA: not significantly enlarged.

Assessment: mildly reduced LV function after NSTEMI with regional wall motion abnormality (inferior wall). No sign of mechanical complication (septal defect, papillary muscle rupture).
Repeat echo recommended in 6–8 weeks.
ACE inhibitor important (continue ramipril, consider increasing the dose).

P002-D012.title: Laboratory, day 2 after PCI
P002-D012.text:
Patient: Wimmer Gerald, born 23.05.1970
Order number: LM-2024-10-16-0088
Sample taken: 16.10.2024, 06:15

Troponin T hs: 5,420 ng/l ↑↑ (peak, expected after NSTEMI)
CK: 1,840 U/l ↑↑ (peak)
CK-MB: 148 U/l ↑↑

Clinical chemistry:
  Creatinine: 1.12 mg/dl [ref: 0.7–1.2] – OK, no contrast damage
  Na: 139 mmol/l, K: 4.2 mmol/l
  Glucose: 8.4 mmol/l
  LDL cholesterol: 3.9 mmol/l (still raised before statin effect)

P002-D013.title: Progress note day 2 – metformin restarted, smoking advice
P002-D013.text:
16.10.2024, 09:00, Dr Krenn

Creatinine stable (1.12 mg/dl, >48 h after contrast) → metformin 1000 mg 1-0-1 restarted.
The patient reports no chest pain since the stent. Still free of symptoms.
ECG: sinus rhythm, no new changes.

Smoking advice: psychologist Tanja Berger (smoking cessation service) saw the patient today. Patient very motivated to stop. Continue nicotine patch; the psychologist recommends an outpatient smoking cessation group after discharge.

The patient also reports that a few months ago he sometimes noticed palpitations, mainly in the evening – never examined, he thought it was harmless. No ECG was ever done for this.

Plan:
- Discharge on 18 or 19.10. if still stable
- Teaching on dual antiplatelet therapy and stent care
- Lab check for atorvastatin in 6 weeks at the GP

P002-D014.title: Discharge medication – order
P002-D014.text:
18.10.2024, 08:00
Senior Dr Reithofer

Medication at discharge:
1. Aspirin 100 mg (Aspirin Cardio) 1-0-0 – dual antiplatelet therapy part 1 (lifelong)
2. Ticagrelor 90 mg (Brilique) 1-0-1 – dual antiplatelet therapy part 2 (at least 12 months after DES)
   WARNING: stop ONLY after talking to a cardiologist!
3. Atorvastatin 80 mg (Sortis) 0-0-1 – high-dose statin after ACS (lifelong)
4. Ramipril 5 mg (Delix) 1-0-0 – heart failure prevention after NSTEMI (EF 45%)
5. Metformin 1000 mg (Glucophage) 1-0-1 – type 2 diabetes

Stopped during the stay:
- Simvastatin 40 mg (replaced by atorvastatin 80 mg)
- Heparin IV
- Nicotine patch: prescribed for another 8 weeks as an outpatient

Note: pause metformin at least 48 h before any contrast examination.

P002-D015.title: Discharge letter after NSTEMI and PCI
P002-D015.text:
Discharge letter
Musterstadt Regional Hospital, Cardiology
Date: 18.10.2024

Dear Dr Holzmann,

We are discharging Mr Gerald Wimmer, born 23.05.1970, after an inpatient stay from 14.10.2024 to 18.10.2024.

Main diagnoses:
1. NSTEMI (inferior wall ischaemia) with proximal LAD stenosis (I21.4)
2. Two-vessel coronary artery disease (LAD critical, RCA moderate)
3. Status after PCI with DES (Orsiro Mission 3.0×18 mm) in the proximal LAD, 14.10.2024
4. Mildly reduced LV function (EF 45%) after NSTEMI
5. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (E11)
6. Arterial hypertension (I10)
7. Dyslipidaemia (E78.5)
8. Nicotine dependence (active smoker, cessation started)

Course:
Emergency admission. Initial diagnosis "suspected STEMI" by the GP; after senior doctor ECG review reclassified as NSTEMI. Urgent coronary angiography on 14.10., PCI with DES in the LAD without problems. Contrast premedication because of a reported contrast reaction (flushing, shortness of breath after iodinated contrast, unconfirmed allergy) – procedure without reaction. Echo after PCI: EF 45%, inferior wall hypokinesia.

Allergy/intolerance note: reported contrast reaction (flushing, shortness of breath) after iodinated contrast – grade I–II, not clinically confirmed (no formal allergy test). For contrast: use premedication and iso-osmolar contrast.

Medication at discharge:
1. Aspirin 100 mg 1-0-0
2. Ticagrelor 90 mg 1-0-1 (at least 12 months, do NOT stop without cardiology!)
3. Atorvastatin 80 mg 0-0-1
4. Ramipril 5 mg 1-0-0
5. Metformin 1000 mg 1-0-1

Nicotine patch 14 mg for another 8 weeks.

Implant: drug-eluting stent (DES) in the proximal LAD: Biotronik Orsiro Mission 3.0×18 mm, sirolimus-coated. Implanted 14.10.2024.

Recommendations:
- Cardiology check in 6 weeks (echo for EF, review of antiplatelet therapy)
- HbA1c and lipids in 6 weeks at the GP
- Smoking cessation group
- Avoid physical strain for 4 weeks, then cardiac rehabilitation

Kind regards, Senior Dr Bernhard Reithofer, cardiologist
Musterstadt Regional Hospital
